motion.name: ease-out
motion.value: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)
motion.purpose: The system easing (--ease-out): buttons, solo fades, draw-in, mobile menu, theme reveal.

motion.name: draw-track
motion.value: 1.6s var(--ease-out), per-line delay 0 to 600ms
motion.purpose: Route map tracks draw in once, when 35% of the map is on screen (data-drawn on the svg), not on load.

motion.name: stop-in
motion.value: 500ms var(--ease-out), staggered 70 to 90ms
motion.purpose: Stations, interchanges and terminus bars fade in after their track.

motion.name: nav-pill-spring
motion.value: spring, stiffness 420, damping 36 (shared layoutId)
motion.purpose: Active-section glass pill moving between nav links; instant under reduced motion.

motion.name: theme-reveal
motion.value: View Transition, clip-path circle from the theme button, 700ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); fallback 400ms colour cross-fade
motion.purpose: Theme switch; theme stored under localStorage "theme", light default.

motion.name: now-pulse
motion.value: 2.4s var(--ease-out) infinite, scale 1 to 2.6
motion.purpose: Ring around the now-station.

motion.name: train-run
motion.value: 3.2s, keySplines 0.45 0 0.2 1, once; SMIL begin indefinite, started via beginElement 1.7s plus the line stagger after the draw
motion.purpose: Two-car train runs each live line and stops at now.

motion.name: solo
motion.value: opacity 220ms var(--ease-out), inactive lines to 0.12, interchanges group to 0.25
motion.purpose: Line solo on hover or focus.

motion.name: press
motion.value: translateY(1px) scale(0.98)
motion.purpose: Button active state.

motion.name: led-scroll
motion.value: 22 columns per second
motion.purpose: LED message scroll when it overflows; disabled under reduced motion. Dot pitch 4px in the hero from sm (3px on phones), 3px in the sticky display and footer.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion gates draw-in, stops, pulse, trains, LED scroll, smooth scroll, the nav pill spring, the circular theme reveal and all scroll choreography
motion.purpose: Accessibility floor.

motion.name: motion-gate
motion.value: html.motion-ok, set by the head script before first paint unless prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
motion.purpose: Every scroll start state lives under it; without it everything is in its final state. useScrollMotion (mounted once in App) exits early without it.

motion.name: reveal-once
motion.value: IntersectionObserver, rootMargin 0px 0px -12% 0px, unobserve after first hit; sets data-shown
motion.purpose: Shared trigger for [data-reveal] kinds. Wipes are observed through their parent (a fully clipped element has no intersection area).

motion.name: reveal-wipe
motion.value: clip-path inset(-0.15em 100% -0.3em -0.1em) to inset(-0.15em -0.15em -0.3em -0.1em), 1100ms var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: Section titles, platform line names, footer headline.

motion.name: reveal-pop
motion.value: scale(0.4) rotate(-120deg), opacity 0 to rest; transform 900ms var(--ease-out), opacity 400ms
motion.purpose: Line roundels on platform signs.

motion.name: reveal-flap
motion.value: perspective(700px) rotateX(-80deg), origin top, to rest; 700ms var(--ease-out), opacity 300ms; delay var(--i) * 90ms
motion.purpose: Departure board rows.

motion.name: reveal-draw
motion.value: stroke-dashoffset 1 to 0 over pathLength 1, 1700ms var(--ease-out), delay var(--d); late parts opacity 500ms + scale 0.6 to 1 800ms, both 1400ms late
motion.purpose: Footer terminus lines; terminus bars and the Your team capsule are the late parts.

motion.name: strip-fill
motion.value: --p = clamp((0.62 * innerHeight - rail top) / rail height, 0, 1) per rAF on scroll; ::after scaleY(var(--p)), 140ms linear, over a ::before ghost at 0.2
motion.purpose: Strip rail drawn as you read against a reading line at 62% of the viewport.

motion.name: stop-reached
motion.value: data-reached when the fill passes the dot (stop top + 20px); dot scale 0.62 to 1 (600ms var(--ease-out)), ring ink 28% to ink (300ms)
motion.purpose: Station arrival on the strip; the current stop fills only once reached.

motion.name: stop-content
motion.value: opacity 0 + translateX(-1.25rem) to rest; opacity 600ms, transform 800ms var(--ease-out), 90ms delay
motion.purpose: Stop text arrives from the rail side.

motion.name: shot-wipe
motion.value: clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0 round 1rem) to inset(0 round 1rem), 1000ms var(--ease-out), 260ms delay
motion.purpose: Stop screenshots open from the rail.

motion.name: terminus-fade
motion.value: opacity clamp(0, (var(--p) - 0.94) * 18, 1)
motion.purpose: An ended line's terminus bar appears as the fill reaches the end.

breakpoints.name: route-map-compact
breakpoints.note: Map column width (ResizeObserver, not viewport). Below it: compact mode, stroke scale k = 2.2, station names and milestone labels hidden; the map never scrolls sideways.

narrative.overview:
The whole site is a KRL Jabodetabek route diagram. One ink person-line runs left to right along a time axis; every job is a coloured line that leaves it at its real start month, carries its products as stations, and either ends at a terminus bar or keeps running past "now". Everything else is station furniture: line badges, platform signs, a strip map down each line, a departure board, an in-car amber LED passenger display, and a night terminus where the running lines arrive. The visitor reads a network, not a portfolio grid.

Density is calm and wide: a cool white ground, big poster type, thick strokes, and generous vertical travel between stops. Colour is never decoration; each hue is a line, and a line's colour only appears where that line is present. Depth is soft and physical (lifted pills, screenshots, boards) over a flat ground; controls and the nav are glass, so the map and lines stay visible through them. Motion belongs to the network and follows the reader: the route map draws itself once it is on screen and its trains run once to "now", each line's strip rail fills as you read down it and stations light up when the train reaches them, board names are unveiled with a wipe, and the departure board flaps its rows down. A pulse rings the now-station, and lines solo on hover or focus. Without motion permission everything simply sits in its final state.

Dark mode is a night platform, not an inverted page: ground goes to deep blue-black, ink to near-white, line colours brighten so they still read as the same lines. The departure board, the LED display and the terminus footer are night objects in both themes.
keyCharacteristics: A time-scaled route map is the signature, in its own section straight after a full-screen station-board hero; everything else (sections, nav, contact) reuses its vocabulary.
One colour per line, applied through a single scoped line-colour variable.
Bonbance condensed poster type for station-board names; BDO Grotesk for every label, body and control.
Round-capped thick strokes, 45 degree bends, ground-filled dots with ink rings, pill shapes for everything interactive.
One glass control family: ink glass primary, clear glass secondary, clear glass round controls and a floating glass nav capsule.
Tabular numerals on every date, count and year.

rules.name: The Line Owns Its Colour Rule
rules.body: A line colour appears only on things that belong to that line: its track, badge, platform sign, strip, current-stop fill, screenshot-switcher selection (the active index fills with the line colour; inactive indexes are clear glass) and link underline. Components read one scoped variable (`--line`) set on the line's container; they never hard-code a line hue. The only multi-line uses are keys to the whole network (the legend and the terminus footer's converging lines).

rules.name: The Night Board Rule
rules.body: The departure board, the LED displays and the night terminus footer stay dark in light and dark themes alike. Amber lives only on them (inside the footer: the LED, the contact-board labels and text selection).

rules.name: The Tabular Timetable Rule
rules.body: Every date, year, count and switcher index sets in tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Poster Name Rule
rules.body: Bonbance is for names on boards (person, sections, lines, line roundels) and nothing smaller than about 1.6rem. Running text, labels and controls are always BDO Grotesk.

rules.name: The Board Caps Rule
rules.body: Uppercase is reserved for transit hardware: the LED display, the departure board's column heads and the footer contact board's field labels. No other uppercase labels.

rules.name: The Lifted Object Rule
rules.body: Shadows belong to things that sit on the platform, never to the ground or to a line's own signage.

rules.name: The One Glass Rule
rules.body: Every control is glass from one family: ink glass for the one primary action, clear glass for secondary actions and round controls, the glass capsule for navigation. New controls join that family rather than adding a flat or outlined variant.

rules.name: The Final State Rule
rules.body: Every choreographed element is authored in its final, readable state; motion only adds a start state under the motion permission class. Without it (reduced motion, or no script) nothing is hidden, clipped or waiting.

dos: Do set a line's colour once, as `--line` on its container, and let badges, strips, dots, platform signs and underlines read it.
Do keep station dots ground-filled with ink rings; fill only the latest stop on a running line.
Do bend lines at 45 degrees only, with round caps and joins.
Do set every date and count in tabular numerals.
Do make every control a full pill (official store badges keep their own artwork), with the 3px Dimensi blue focus ring at 3px offset.

Do let the route map and the timetable fit their column; below 720px the map switches to compact mode (2.2x strokes, names hidden) and on phones the timetable folds its dates under the role, instead of scrolling sideways.
Do build every new control from the glass family (ink glass, clear glass, Glass Control), with its dark variant.

Do gate draw-in, trains, pulse, LED scrolling, the nav pill spring, the circular theme reveal and all scroll choreography behind reduced motion; scroll start states exist only under the motion permission class, so the default is the final state.
Do build new scroll reveals from the existing kinds (wipe, pop, flap, draw, rail), revealed once on entry.
Do use the real theSVG brand logo on tech chips.
donts: Don't use a line colour for anything that isn't that line, and don't add a line colour without a real job behind it.
Don't use amber anywhere except the LED displays, the departure board and the night terminus footer.
Don't set running text, labels or controls in Bonbance.
Don't add uppercase tracked labels outside the board and LED hardware.
Don't put shadows on the ground, platform signs or strips, and don't use hard offset shadows.
Don't fall back to same-size project cards or a skills bento; products are stations on their line.
